newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES STRIKE AGAIN IN LAST AT-BAT TO BEAT PADRES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES STRIKE AGAIN IN LAST AT-BAT TO BEAT PADRES.

text.p: Andruw Jones's two-run homer off Trevor Hoffman in the bottom of the 10th inning gave the rampaging Braves a 3-2 victory Saturday over the San Diego Padres in another case of late-inning heroics.

The home run by Jones came after Kenny Lofton reached second on a single and an error by right fielder Tony Gwynn. The victory was the Braves' fourth earned in their final at-bat this season and 10th in 11 games at Turner Field.
"Before I go out there, I asked Bobby (Braves manager Bobby Cox) if I should bunt him over," Jones said. "He said, No, swing.' They expected a bunt and he threw me a fastball right in the middle."
Hoffman (0-1) suffered his second blown save in five chances as San Diego dropped its fourth straight.
The Padres took the lead in the top of the 10th off Mark Wohlers when Rickey Henderson drew a two-out walk and scored as Ryan Klesko bobbled Quilvio Veras's double down the left-field line.
The defending National League champion Braves improved to a major-league best 16-5.

In Houston, Shawn Estes took a no-hitter into the sixth inning and went the distance on a brilliant two-hitter for his first career shutout as the San Francisco Giants defeated the Houston Astros 2-0.
Estes (4-0), who allowed only singles to Pat Listach and Tony Eusebio, also recorded his first career complete game for the surprising Giants, who improved to 15-5.
"It felt good tonight," said Estes, 24, who was backed by a pair of second-inning runs. "This is my first complete game since high school."
"He had it on tonight," Giants manager Dusty Baker said.

In Chicago, Sammy Sosa delivered a one-out RBI single in the bottom of the eighth inning as the Chicago Cubs rallied from a four-run deficit for their second successive win, 7-6 over the Pittsburgh Pirates.
Bob Patterson (1-1) worked a scoreless eighth for the win and Mel Rojas, Chicago's seventh pitcher, retired all three batters in the ninth for his first save as a Cub.
"It's great to get my first save," said Rojas. "I wasn't sure if it was going to come or not."

Chicago has won its last two games at Wrigley Field after opening the season with seven straight home losses. The Cubs also improved to 4-3 since setting a National League record with 14 consecutive losses to start the season.
Chicago's Ryne Sandberg broke Joe Morgan's record for home runs by a second baseman with a solo shot in the second inning. It was Sandberg's 267th home run as a second baseman and his 272nd overall.

In Montreal, Pedro Martinez continued his mastery of the Mets and Darrin Fletcher capped a five-run fifth inning with a two-run homer as the Montreal Expos won their sixth straight game, 8-1 over New York.

Martinez (3-0) gave up four hits and one unearned run in seven innings with 10 strikeouts to lower his ERA to 0.44 (one earned run in 20 1/3 innings). The right-hander improved to 10-0 lifetime against the Mets.
"I know by now how well I've done against that team and it does give me a litte more confidence than usual," said Martinez.

In St Louis, Dante Bichette had three RBI, including a two-run double in a three-run fourth inning, and Bill Swift threw six shutout innings as the Colorado Rockies continued their surprising road play by beating the Cardinals 4-2.
Swift (2-1) allowed just two hits in his first start in 13 days since he was scratched from his April 20 start due to a small tear of his right pectoral muscle.
The Rockies (15-5) won their fifth straight game overall and have won their last eight road games. Colorado went 28-53 on the road last year.

In Cincinnati, Hal Morris, Eddie Taubensee and starting pitcher Pete Schourek all homered against Curt Schilling as the Cincinnati Reds halted their five-game losing streak with a 10-2 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Schourek (1-2) allowed two runs -- one earned -- and two hits in five innings on his way to his first win in nearly a year and he improved to 7-3 lifetime against Philadelphia.
Schilling (3-2) was tagged for six runs and six hits in four innings. "I'm embarrassed by what I did," Schilling said. "I didn't have my best stuff, but that's no excuse not to win."
At Florida, Jeff Conine hit a two-run homer and Charles Johnson added a three-run shot as the Florida Marlins won their fourth straight home game, defeating the Los Angeles Dodgers 8-3.

Florida starter Alex Fernandez (3-2) snapped a personal two-game losing streak by allowing three runs and six hits over 5 1/3 innings. Dennis Cook, Mark Hutton and Jay Powell held Los Angeles scoreless over the final 3 2/3 innings.
Ismael Valdes (1-3) took the loss.
